metadata.track: Social Engineering Attack Simulations Using Python (Day 05)

target_profile.name: Harish Kumar
target_profile.bio: Senior Cloud Security Engineer & Backend Dev. Building resilient identity pipelines.

spear_phishing_pretexts.title: Technical Zero-Day CVE Alert (Python Ecosystem)
spear_phishing_pretexts.pretext: Adversary impersonates GitHub Security Advisories or the Python core security team. They send an urgent notification citing an unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in dependency trees matching repository 'cloud-guard-iam'.
spear_phishing_pretexts.call_to_action: Click link to review affected dependency tree: https://security-patch-advisory.org/cve/cloud-guard-iam

spear_phishing_pretexts.title: Corporate Workspace Re-Authentication (Sqrock IT Solution)
spear_phishing_pretexts.pretext: Leveraging the public exposure of employer 'Sqrock IT Solution' and location 'Bangalore, India', attacker impersonates Sqrock IT Solution IT Operations. They notify Harish Kumar that their corporate VPN/SSO certificate is pending mandatory migration before the end of the business day.
spear_phishing_pretexts.hook: Sqrock IT Solution IT Notice: Mandatory Single Sign-On Endpoint Renewal
spear_phishing_pretexts.call_to_action: Authenticate your identity via the corporate portal: https://login.sqrockitsolution-portal.net/sso

spear_phishing_pretexts.title: Targeted Executive / Recruiter Headhunting Hook (Python Specialist)
spear_phishing_pretexts.pretext: Attacker poses as an executive talent scout from a high-profile technology firm, praising Harish Kumar's open-source contributions in Python. They attach a weaponized PDF or link purporting to be a confidential compensation structure and technical architecture brief.
spear_phishing_pretexts.hook: Confidential Senior Python Architecture Lead Opportunity for Harish Kumar

defensive_opsec_evaluation.exposure_summary: Severe identity exposure. Direct personal email, employer, and activity patterns enable multi-stage targeted whaling/vishing.

risk_factors.risk: Enables corporate authority & IT helpdesk pretexting
Permits targeted timezone and regional event pretexting
Bypasses web contact forms; direct spear-phishing inbox vector
Provides secondary attack surfaces and credential harvesting avenues
Reveals current active projects and psychological triggers
